title: Transforms, anchors and pivots
summary: Position, rotate and scale entities using local coordinates, world pivots and geometry anchors.

blocks.text: `move` sets a position and `shift` adds an offset. Direct entity methods change state immediately; `entity.animate` records target changes into an Animator for Scene.play. Transform also exposes local and world variants for rotations, shifts and scaling. A world-space operation accounts for the parent matrix rather than treating the world point as a local coordinate.

Be careful when selecting an anchor: `Entity.move` adjusts the target so the chosen bounds point lands there, while `Entity.setPosition` sets a pivot before assigning translation. They do not have identical anchor behavior in the current implementation. Likewise, `Entity.rotate` and `Entity.scale` accumulate changes; `Entity.setRotation` and `Entity.setScale` assign absolute values, which is usually what a slider needs.
Compare a local edge with a world pivot

Both rectangles rotate around a marked point. The left point is selected from the rectangle’s local edge before rotation; the right point is supplied as a world coordinate. Click a rectangle to reverse direction.

An anchor selects a persistent position relative to the object’s own bounds, such as LEFT or CENTER. A pivot identifies the point about which rotation or scaling occurs. Setting a world pivot also needs to preserve the object’s current visual placement through offset synchronization. They should not be used interchangeably.

Anchoring text to CENTER makes its center the placement reference. Use nextTo and alignTo when positions should follow measured bounds. Intrinsic geometry can change after font loading, a Tex rebuild or a layout update, so measure after those operations are ready.
